why: All three legs survive. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/large-codebases.md line 155 carries the quoted text exactly, as sentences 2 and 3 of a three-sentence line. The whole line reads: 'Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded, so organization-wide instructions always apply. You can set `claudeMdExcludes` at any [settings scope](/docs/en/settings#configuration-scopes): user, project, local, or managed. Arrays merge across scopes, so a team can set project-level defaults while individuals add local overrides.' The first sentence narrows managed CLAUDE.md files from being excludable; it does not reverse the scope-merge claim. (2) CODE: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/instruction-excludes.ts:60-80 getConfiguredInstructionExcludes() calls loadStoredConfig() and merges only the two key spellings ('instructionExcludes', 'claudeMdExcludes', line 28) inside that one object. loadStoredConfig (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:793, cited as :788 - line-number drift only) reads exactly one file, CONFIG_FILE = join(CONFIG_DIR, 'config.json') at :152 (cited :147), and CONFIG_DIR is the user-level ~/.nessy-agent (config/paths.ts:21). The one injection seam, env.instructionExcludes (capabilities/native-sources.ts:890), is confirmed test-only with grep -a: the sole production caller is packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:641 passing `deps.nativeSourcesEnv ?? {}`, and every setter of nativeSourcesEnv is a __tests__ file, none of which is a production path. base-agent.ts:1242-1243 (the lazy nested-instruction channel) calls getConfiguredInstructionExcludes() with no env override at all. (3) CONSEQUENCE, tested separately from the identifier: the fork DOES read project- and local-scope Claude settings files - native-sources.ts:1046-1056 registers .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json, and permissions-config.ts:500-530 (claudeSettingsPermissionDsl) parses them - but ONLY their `permissions` block. grep -ran over packages/ apps/ (NUL-safe) finds zero readers of claudeMdExcludes outside instruction-excludes.ts, native-sources.ts, base-agent.ts and comments, so a claudeMdExcludes array in a project or local settings file is parsed by nothing and merges with nothing. The Nessy-native project tier (native-sources.ts:1013-1042: .nessy-agent/skills, agents, mcp.json, hooks.json, permissions.json, MEMORY.md, rules) has no settings/config file that could carry the key either, so there is no renamed project-scope equivalent. Neither an owner decision (not among the nine in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3) nor a product difference (nothing to do with the de-brand, the dropped subscription providers or the corporate gateway); the R28 plan that built the matcher, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-rules-tier.md:31, only specifies the glob semantics and records no scope decision.
correctedState: Instruction/rule exclusion patterns are read from exactly one user-level file, CONFIG_DIR/config.json (~/.nessy-agent/config.json), where the two key spellings `instructionExcludes` and `claudeMdExcludes` merge with each other (instruction-excludes.ts:60-80, INSTRUCTION_EXCLUDE_SETTING_KEYS at :28). No project-, local- or managed-scope source is consulted: .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json are read only for their `permissions` block (permissions-config.ts:500-530), the .nessy-agent project tier has no settings file at all, and env.instructionExcludes - the only other seam - has no production writer (storage-runtime.ts:641 always passes an env with no such key). The documented cross-scope merge is therefore absent for the native pipeline that actually injects instruction, memory and rule files on both backends (buildNativeCapabilityInventory's final filter at native-sources.ts:1128-1134, plus BaseAgent's lazy nested-instruction matcher at base-agent.ts:1242). One nuance worth recording, which narrows but does not refute the finding: on the opt-in Claude backend the SDK is handed settingSources: ['user','project','local'] (claude-agent.ts:305), so the native claude binary applies scoped claudeMdExcludes to the CLAUDE.md files IT discovers - but Nessy's own pinned capability block, which runs on that backend too, re-injects the very files that scoped exclusion was meant to drop.
